variants.message:
Chase, Go-Forth's range of home services makes the handoff from a customer's first request an interesting place for AI. I'd like to help the receiving team get the context as well as the assignment.

I'm {sender} at Nine-67; our engineers build with operating teams.

Is that handoff already working as well as you'd like?

variants.label: Business idea
variants.subject: the right team with the right context
variants.message:
Chase, we'd build an intake brief from the customer's request: service needed, information already given and questions still open. Go-Forth's team would review it before routing the job. Nine-67 handles the AI build and training.

Would an example of that handoff be useful?

variants.label: With proof
variants.subject: one application your team helps shape
variants.message:
Chase, Nine-67 recently helped one client deploy 20 applications, working with users from first build through training. We're an AI-first engineering team.

At Go-Forth, I'd explore one intake-to-service handoff so the customer's context reaches the right team.

Would you like a short plan for that application?

variants.label: Wildcard
variants.subject: don't make the customer start over
variants.message:
Chase, I'd give AI the job of making sure the next team already knows the customer's story.

Our engineers at Nine-67 could turn Go-Forth's intake notes into a brief with the request, open questions and next step for review.

Would that be a welcome improvement for your service teams?

variants.label: Personal
variants.subject: before the estimator starts
variants.message:
Joseph, Michigan Box serves food and industrial customers, so I'd like to help with the details an estimator needs before pricing a request.

I'm {sender} at Nine-67. Our AI engineers could check the incoming specifications and prepare missing-information questions for your team.

Is that clarification work a meaningful part of the quoting process?

variants.label: Business idea
variants.subject: an RFQ ready to price
variants.message:
Joseph, we'd build an RFQ check that extracts packaging specifications, compares them with your requirements and flags what's missing before estimating. Nine-67 would build with Michigan Box's team and measure review time and clarification rounds.

Would a sample RFQ walkthrough be useful?

variants.label: With proof
variants.subject: AI before the pricing decision
variants.message:
Joseph, Nine-67 has built a proposal workspace that brings requirements and approved information together for review. We're an AI-first engineering team.

I'd apply that checking approach before Michigan Box's estimators price an RFQ, with your team approving the interpretation.

Would you like to see the requirements-review step?

variants.label: Wildcard
variants.subject: give AI the incomplete request
variants.message:
Joseph, I'd hand AI the incomplete RFQ and ask it to come back with better questions.

Our engineers at Nine-67 could build that check around Michigan Box's packaging requirements. The estimator gets a clearer request to price.

Would that take worthwhile work off the quoting desk?

variants.label: Personal
variants.subject: finding the right coil match
variants.message:
Jim, Almetals' processing and distribution work looks like a practical place to help with the checking before a quote.

I'm {sender} at Nine-67. Our AI engineers could assemble stock options and supporting specifications for your team's review.

Is finding the match or confirming the documentation the larger task?

variants.label: Business idea
variants.subject: prepare the match before the quote
variants.message:
Jim, we'd build a request check for one Almetals alloy family: extract the gauge and other requirements, prepare stock options and attach the relevant documents. Your team approves the match. Nine-67 handles the AI engineering.

Would a sample request-to-review walkthrough be worth sending?

variants.label: With proof
variants.subject: checking the requirements first
variants.message:
Jim, our proposal workspace at Nine-67 brings requirements and approved information together so reviewers can check the result. We're an AI-first engineering team.

At Almetals, I'd explore that same evidence-gathering step around a stock match.

Would you like to see the review approach?

variants.label: Wildcard
variants.subject: almost right isn't the match
variants.message:
Jim, I'd give AI the job of showing its work on a metal match: here's the request, here's the stock and here's the supporting specification.

Nine-67's engineers would build it with Almetals' team, who make the approval.

Would that help your quoting process?

variants.label: Personal
variants.subject: before the next stock decision
variants.message:
John, I'd like to help English Gardens' buyers see available stock across locations before making the next replenishment decision.

I'm {sender} at Nine-67. Our AI engineers build with operating teams to gather the information behind those calls.

Is preparing that comparison already straightforward for your buyers?

variants.label: Business idea
variants.subject: check another location first
variants.message:
John, we'd build a category review that brings demand and available stock together, including what another English Gardens location has. Buyers review the suggested checks and make the decisions. Nine-67 would measure preparation time with the team.

Would a sample review for one category be useful?

variants.label: With proof
variants.subject: a practical first application
variants.message:
John, Nine-67 has deployed a resource-allocation application with a client, building it with the people making the decisions. We're an AI-first engineering team.

I'd explore a different allocation task at English Gardens: preparing the stock comparison for buyers.

Would you like an outline of how that review could work?

variants.label: Wildcard
variants.subject: the stock might already be yours
variants.message:
John, the stock a buyer needs might already belong to English Gardens, just at another location.

I'd put AI on getting that comparison ready. Our engineers at Nine-67 would build with your buyers and leave the purchasing decisions with them.

Would that save useful preparation in a seasonal category?

variants.label: Personal
variants.subject: keeping the service history useful
variants.message:
Jerry, Braman's Fusion acquisition made me think about keeping customer history useful as records change hands, particularly promises still open.

I'm {sender} at Nine-67. Our AI engineers build tools that assemble that history for the receiving service team.

Is that handoff still relevant, or already settled?

variants.label: Business idea
variants.subject: the commitments inside the records
variants.message:
Jerry, we'd build a customer handoff brief from service history and unresolved commitments, with links back to the original records. Nine-67's AI engineers would work with Braman's receiving team and check completeness.

Would a sample of that brief be useful for future acquisition handoffs?

variants.label: With proof
variants.subject: a working view of customer history
variants.message:
Jerry, Nine-67 deployed an account-health view for a professional-services firm, bringing account concerns and business context together. We're an AI-first engineering company.

I'd explore that approach for service teams receiving customer records at Braman.

Would you like to see the account view as an example?

variants.label: Wildcard
variants.subject: what did we promise this customer
variants.message:
Jerry, I'd want AI to find the promises tucked inside a customer history before the account changes hands.

Our engineers at Nine-67 could build that check with Braman's team, keeping the source record beside each open commitment.

Would that be useful in your next service handoff?

variants.label: Personal
variants.subject: after the inspection finding
variants.message:
Jason, I'd like to help Versacor's team connect an inspection finding with the evidence that the follow-up is complete.

I'm {sender} at Nine-67. Our AI engineers could gather the records and flag incomplete cases for your specialists to check.

Is collecting that evidence a meaningful part of your team's workload?

variants.label: Business idea
variants.subject: make completion easy to verify
variants.message:
Jason, we'd build a follow-up check that puts each finding, responsible person and completion evidence together. Nine-67 would work with Versacor's specialists and measure preparation time and missing records they catch.

Would a sample review of that workflow be useful?

variants.label: With proof
variants.subject: bringing the evidence together
variants.message:
Jason, Nine-67 built a proposal workspace joining requirements, approved information and review. We're an AI-first engineering team.

Versacor's inspection follow-up is a different workflow, but linking a requirement to its supporting evidence could help there too.

Would you like to see that review step?

variants.label: Wildcard
variants.subject: done, with the evidence
variants.message:
Jason, I'd ask AI to bring the evidence when it says an action is done.

Our engineers at Nine-67 could build a follow-up check for Versacor that puts the finding and completion record together for a specialist to approve.

Would that take useful checking off the team's plate?

variants.label: Personal
variants.subject: from the first call to the visit
variants.message:
Luke, Native's move to a chief revenue officer role made me think about the promise that travels from the first call into service.

I'm {sender} at Nine-67. Our AI engineers build with operations teams to keep that context available.

Is the intake-to-service handoff a priority at Native?

variants.label: Business idea
variants.subject: carry the promise into service
variants.message:
Luke, we'd build a first-visit brief from intake notes: what the customer expects, what was promised and what still needs answering. Native's team reviews it before the visit. Nine-67's AI engineers would check completeness and preparation time.

Would a sample brief be useful?

variants.label: With proof
variants.subject: one build that connects the teams
variants.message:
Luke, Nine-67 recently helped one client deploy 20 applications, building with business teams and training them through rollout. We're an AI-first engineering company.

For Native, I'd start between the first customer conversation and the first visit.

Would you like an outline of that handoff application?

variants.label: Wildcard
variants.subject: the promise should travel
variants.message:
Luke, I'd give AI the job of remembering the promises, with the source note attached.

Our engineers at Nine-67 could build a first-visit brief so Native's service team sees what the customer was told and what remains open.

Would that help connect your revenue and service teams?
